tools.name: calculate_break_even
tools.desc: From fixed costs, the variable cost per unit, and the selling price per unit, compute the break-even point: the unit cou
tools.description: From fixed costs, the variable cost per unit, and the selling price per unit, compute the break-even point: the unit count and revenue at which profit is exactly zero. The price must exceed the variable cost, since otherwise every unit sold loses money and break-even is never reached no matter the volume. Optionally pass a sales volume to also get the profit (or loss) at that volume and the margin of safety above break-even. Pure arithmetic, no live cost/pricing feed.

tools.desc: Solve a pricing triangle: given exactly two of cost, price, gross margin percent, and markup percent, derive the other t
tools.description: Solve a pricing triangle: given exactly two of cost, price, gross margin percent, and markup percent, derive the other two plus the gross profit. Margin is profit as a share of the selling price (profit / price) while markup is profit as a share of the cost (profit / cost), so a 20% margin equals a 25% markup. Margin plus markup alone cannot be solved, since neither carries an absolute amount.

parameters.name: markupPercent

parameters.description: Selling price (what the customer pays). Provide exactly two of the four fields.

tools.description: Create a structured workout in Garmin Connect: always a new one, never an edit.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: Ordered steps, each with "type" (warmup, interval, recovery, rest, cooldown or repeat) and exactly one of "duration_seconds", "distance_meters" or "until_lap": true (ends on the lap button: a walk recovery between strides, a warm-up by feel, a rep to a landmark). A repeat is {"type": "repeat", "times": 5, "steps": [...]} and can't contain another repeat. Optional target: "pace" ("4:05" or ["4:00", "4:10"], min/km), "hr" ([150, 165] bpm, or their Garmin zone: "z2", "z3-z4") or "power" (watts, 250 or [240, 260]; a share of the FTP set in Garmin, "95%" or ["88%", "94%"]; or a power zone, "z3"). By default only the work reps carry a target (pace for a run); warm-ups, cool-downs and recoveries carry none, and the description says what easy pace to run them at: marathon pace plus 45-75 s/km, from get_fitness. The watch beeps off target, so a pace target is never narrower than 5 s/km either side ("4:00" becomes 3:55-4:05; tighter is widened around its middle): about 5 either side for reps, 10 for tempo and threshold, 15-20 for steady and long runs, or heart rate for easy running. A ride uses power on the work steps when the rider has a power meter or smart trainer (power shows on rides in get_activities) and an FTP (get_fitness): sweet spot 88-94%, threshold 95-105%, VO2 max 106-120%, endurance 56-75%. One value becomes a range 5% either side. Without a power meter, heart rate. E.g. 15 min warm-up, 5 x 1 km at 4:05, 90 s recoveries, 10 min cool-down: [{"type": "warmup", "duration_seconds": 900}, {"type": "repeat", "times": 5, "steps": [{"type": "interval", "distance_meters": 1000, "pace": "4:05"}, {"type": "recovery", "duration_seconds": 90}]}, {"type": "cooldown", "duration_seconds": 600}]

tools.name: hasdata_duckduckgo_serp_getSearchResults
tools.desc:
Get DuckDuckGo Search Results

Fetches DuckDuckGo SERPs for a query with region targeting (kl, or cc+setLang), safesearc
tools.description:
Get DuckDuckGo Search Results

Fetches DuckDuckGo SERPs for a query with region targeting (kl, or cc+setLang), safesearch (off/moderate/strict), device type, and token-based pagination. Returns organic results (title, url, snippet, displayed url, position, date, sitelinks, video metadata), ads, and the Search Assist AI answer. Use for SEO rank tracking, SERP feature monitoring, DuckDuckGo-specific visibility audits, and training/eval data for search agents.

parameters.name: cc
parameters.description: The two-letter country code for the country to search from. Combined with `setLang` to form the DuckDuckGo region. Ignored if `kl` is set.

parameters.name: deviceType
parameters.description: Specify the device type for the search.

parameters.name: kl
parameters.description: DuckDuckGo region code in `<country>-<language>` form (e.g. `us-en`, `de-de`). Sets country and interface language at once; takes precedence over `cc`/`setLang`. Use `wt-wt` for no region.

parameters.name: nextPageToken
parameters.description: Opaque token returned in each response as `nextPageToken`. Pass it back (in place of `q`) to fetch the next page of results. It carries a pre-signed page URL bound to the original request's session, so it must be used as-is and cannot be constructed manually. Absent when there are no further pages.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Specify the search term for which you want to scrape the SERP. Required unless `nextPageToken` is provided (which carries the query of the page it continues).

parameters.name: safeSearch
parameters.description: Adult Content Filtering option.

parameters.name: setLang
parameters.description: The preferred result/interface language code — usually two letters (e.g. `en`, `de`), with script-tag variants for some languages (e.g. `zh-hans`, `zh-hant`). Combined with `cc` to form the DuckDuckGo region. Ignored if `kl` is set.

Fetches a Glassdoor job posting by its vacancy URL. Returns job title, company name and rating, location, salary estimate, posted date, full job description, and qualifications/benefits. Use for ATS ingestion, job aggregators, comp benchmarking, enrichment of company profiles, and feeding descriptions into LLM matching or resume-tailoring pipelines.

tools.name: hasdata_glassdoor_listing_getJobListings
tools.desc:
Get GlassDoor Job Listings

Searches Glassdoor job listings by keyword and location with sort (recent/relevant), domain
tools.description:
Get GlassDoor Job Listings

Searches Glassdoor job listings by keyword and location with sort (recent/relevant), domain targeting, filters (date posted, distance, salary range, company rating, easy apply, remote), and nextPageToken pagination that keeps the filters. Returns an array of jobs with title, company, location, salary estimate, posted date, job URL, and jobId, plus per-page tokens. Use to build job feeds, monitor hiring trends for roles/companies/regions, power candidate sourcing tools, and collect URLs for downstream full-detail scraping via the Glassdoor Job endpoint.

parameters.name: datePosted
parameters.description: Returns only jobs posted within the given number of days.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The domain of the Glassdoor site (optional).

parameters.name: easyApplyOnly
parameters.description: Returns only jobs that can be applied to directly on Glassdoor. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: The keyword used to search for job listings.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The location to search for job listings.

parameters.name: maxSalary
parameters.description: Upper bound of the yearly pay range, must be greater than `minSalary`. Can be used on its own.

parameters.name: minRating
parameters.description: Returns jobs from companies rated at least this high. Glassdoor applies the filter approximately, so a few companies rated slightly below the value can appear.

parameters.name: minSalary
parameters.description: Lower bound of the yearly pay range. A job is kept when its estimated pay range overlaps the requested one; hourly and monthly pay are converted to yearly. Jobs without a pay estimate are excluded when a salary filter is set.

parameters.name: nextPageToken
parameters.description: Token for fetching the next page of jobs, taken from the pagination of a previous response. The token keeps the filters of the search it came from, so they do not need to be sent again.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Search radius around the location, in miles. `0` keeps only jobs in the location itself. Glassdoor uses 25 miles when this is not set.

parameters.name: remoteOnly
parameters.description: Returns only remote jobs. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The sorting option for the search results.

tools.name: tool_capture_window
tools.desc: Capture a window screenshot and SAVE IT TO A FILE. Provide hwnd or title substring. Crops to the window's CLIENT area by
tools.description: Capture a window screenshot and SAVE IT TO A FILE. Provide hwnd or title substring. Crops to the window's CLIENT area by default, so image pixel (0,0) is the same point click_at calls (0,0) — no frame offset to guess. Returns bounds = the screen rect (x,y,width,height) the image maps to, plus `scale` (multiply image pixels by it to get screen pixels; 1.0 unless you asked for downscaling). Also reports dpi_verified; when false, image pixels and input coordinates cannot be safely paired. Defaults to JPEG q80 — a 1080p shot is ~6-10x smaller than PNG, which is what keeps a long session's request body under the provider's 32 MiB cap. The bytes are NOT inlined as base64 by default (that costs ~12,500 tokens per shot as text); read the saved_path with read_image instead, which attaches the same picture for ~50 tokens. Pass include_data_uri=true only when a caller genuinely cannot read a file. Read-only — no input injection, no focus change.

tools.name: tool_click_at
tools.desc: Click at client-area coordinates within a window. Coordinates relative to window content area (0,0 = top-left). Tries th
tools.description: Click at client-area coordinates within a window. Coordinates relative to window content area (0,0 = top-left). Tries the ELEMENT path first (resolve the point via UI Automation and invoke that element) because it needs no focus and does not care about z-order; falls back to a raw cursor click, which does. The result's `method` says which was used: 'ax_press' or 'raw_event'. MUTATING: serialized across agent sessions; the raw_event path ALSO YIELDS TO THE USER (waits for input-quiet, then refuses with user-active rather than fighting them for the cursor); the ax_press path injects no physical input. The raw path verifies the addressed window actually owns that screen point and returns success=false instead of clicking another window. Pass dry_run=true to check where the click would land without moving the cursor, clicking, or taking any gate.

MUTATING: serialized across agent sessions via the admission gate, and global hotkeys additionally YIELD TO THE USER — recent mouse/keyboard activity makes them wait, then refuse with reason user-active instead of interrupting; switch to element actions or retry later. Also refuses when the window is not the foreground window, because injected keys would go to the wrong window.

tools.name: tool_skyshot
tools.desc: Read a window's UI as a compact TEXT tree instead of a screenshot — far cheaper than an image, and it names elements a h
tools.description: Read a window's UI as a compact TEXT tree instead of a screenshot — far cheaper than an image, and it names elements a hit-test cannot reach (e.g. an input inside a Chromium page, which element_at_point reports only as the enclosing 'document'). Each line is '{index} {indent}{role} {name}{Value: ...}{(state)}'. Every shot after the first is a DIFF against the previous one: unchanged lines are omitted, '~' marks a changed line, '+' an added one, and removed indices are summarised as ranges. So a second call is usually a few lines, not the whole tree — an unchanged window costs about 100 characters. INDEXES ARE POSITIONAL: each shot numbers the tree it just walked, so a number is only valid against the shot that printed it. '~' and '+' lines carry THIS shot's index and may be acted on; unchanged lines carry no index, so reaching one needs disable_diff=true for a full render. An index read from an older shot is not a durable handle — re-check it with a fresh shot before acting if the window may have changed. The result includes shot_key (the window the diff baseline belongs to — the baseline lives server-side and outlives your session, so this is how you confirm it was taken against the window you meant). Pass include_offscreen=true to include elements that are scrolled out or hidden. The result reports `minimized`, because a minimized window does not always expose its full tree (measured on Edge and on Explorer; Notepad was unaffected) — so a small tree is not proof that the window is empty, and include_offscreen does not recover it. Restore the window once and read again if the result matters. NOTE: this reads element VALUES, so the text can contain whatever is on screen in that window. Read-only — no input injection, no focus change; safe to call while the user works.

tools.name: tool_type_text
tools.desc: Type a text string into a window character-by-character (window-targeted PostMessage, not global keystrokes). The text c
tools.description: Type a text string into a window character-by-character (window-targeted PostMessage, not global keystrokes). The text control inside the window is resolved automatically — a top-level window does not forward WM_CHAR to its child edit, so passing a window handle alone used to post into nothing — and the control's text is read back so `effect_verified` says whether the text actually landed. MUTATING (soft): serialized across agent sessions; no physical input is injected so it can run while the user types — but the window may be RAISED to foreground, so avoid typing into a window the user is currently working in.

Use to keep external systems in sync (restart a service after rotation, post to Slack on delete, kick a build); prefer `agent_remember` for storing facts an agent should recall later, and `register_hook` is not the right tool for time-based scheduled rotation (use `agent_scan` for that). Mutates the hook registry on disk. At least one match criterion (`key`, `keyPattern`, or `tag`) is required — calls without any return an error. Returns JSON of the registered hook entry including its assigned `id` (use that `id` with `remove_hook`).

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: Which lifecycle actions trigger this hook. Defaults to all three.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Required when type='shell'. The literal shell command to run; q-ring exposes the matching key as $QRING_HOOK_KEY and action as $QRING_HOOK_ACTION.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Free-text human-readable description, surfaced by `list_hooks` and the dashboard.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Trigger only on this exact key name. Pick at most one of `key` / `keyPattern` / `tag` (or combine for stricter matching).

parameters.name: keyPattern
parameters.description: Trigger on any key matching this glob pattern. Examples: 'DB_*', 'STRIPE_*'.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Restrict the hook to secrets in this scope. Omit to fire across both global and project secrets.

parameters.name: signalName
parameters.description: Signal name to send (e.g. 'SIGHUP', 'SIGUSR1'). Defaults to SIGHUP, which most daemons treat as 'reload config'.

parameters.name: signalTarget
parameters.description: Required when type='signal'. Either a numeric PID or a process name resolvable via `ps`.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Trigger on any secret carrying this exact tag. Combinable with key/keyPattern as an AND filter.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Hook delivery mechanism. 'shell' runs a local command, 'http' POSTs JSON to a URL, 'signal' sends an OS signal to a named process.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Required when type='http'. Full URL to POST a JSON body `{ id, key, scope, action, timestamp }` to (the value itself is never sent).

tools.name: remove_hook
tools.desc: [hooks] Detach a single lifecycle hook by its registry id so it stops firing. Use to retire a specific webhook/command w
tools.description: [hooks] Detach a single lifecycle hook by its registry id so it stops firing. Use to retire a specific webhook/command without touching any secrets; prefer `delete_secret` to remove a credential and `tunnel_destroy` for ephemeral tunnels. Mutates the hook registry only — does not touch secret values, audit log, or env states. Idempotent in spirit: removing an already-absent id returns a not-found error rather than partial work. Returns 'Removed hook ID' on success.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Hook id returned by `register_hook` or visible in `list_hooks` (opaque string).

tools.name: rotate_secret
tools.desc: [validation] Ask the upstream provider to issue a fresh credential for this secret and store the new value back into the
tools.description: [validation] Ask the upstream provider to issue a fresh credential for this secret and store the new value back into the keyring. Use when a secret is expiring, leaked, or part of a scheduled rotation; prefer `generate_secret` for self-managed values you fully control, and `agent_scan --autoRotate` for sweep-style rotation across multiple expired keys. Mutates the keyring with the newly-issued value if rotation succeeds (one 'write' audit event), and makes outbound network requests against the provider's rotation API. Returns JSON `{ rotated, newValue?, message?, ... }`. If `rotated` is false, the existing value is left untouched.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Exact key to rotate. Must already exist in the keyring.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Organization identifier for org-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='org'. Example: 'acme-corp'.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root for project-scoped secrets and policy resolution. Defaults to the MCP server's current working directory when omitted.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Force a specific provider id (see `list_providers`). Omit to auto-detect from the current value or the secret's stored provider hint.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where the secret lives. 'global' = user keyring (default if omitted on reads), 'project' = scoped to projectPath, 'team' = team-shared (needs teamId), 'org' = org-shared (needs orgId).

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Team identifier for team-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='team'. Example: 'acme-platform'.

tools.desc: [scan] Walk a directory tree and flag plausible hardcoded secrets using regex heuristics plus Shannon-entropy scoring on
tools.description: [scan] Walk a directory tree and flag plausible hardcoded secrets using regex heuristics plus Shannon-entropy scoring on string literals. Use as a one-shot 'is anything leaking in this repo?' audit before commit/release; prefer `lint_files` when you already know the specific files to check (and want optional auto-fix). Read-only — never modifies source files. Honors `.gitignore`. Returns JSON array of `{ file, line, key, value, kind }` findings, or 'No hardcoded secrets found in the specified directory.' when clean. False positives are possible — review before treating as ground truth.

parameters.name: dirPath
parameters.description: Directory to scan, absolute or relative to the server cwd. The scan recurses into subdirectories.

tools.name: set_secret
tools.desc: [secrets] Create or overwrite a single secret value, optionally with TTL/decay, per-env superposition, description, tags
tools.description: [secrets] Create or overwrite a single secret value, optionally with TTL/decay, per-env superposition, description, tags, and rotation hints. Use to add or update one key at a time; prefer `import_dotenv` for bulk .env ingest, `generate_secret` (with saveAs) to generate-and-store in one step, and `entangle_secrets` instead of duplicating the same value under two keys. Mutates the keyring (overwrites any existing value at the same key/scope), writes a 'write' event to the audit log, and triggers any matching hooks. Subject to tool policy. Returns a short confirmation text like '[scope] KEY saved' (or '[scope] KEY set for env:NAME' when `env` is provided).

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Free-text human-readable description shown in `inspect_secret` and the dashboard.

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: If set, writes this value to the named per-env state (superposition) instead of the default slot. Existing default value is preserved as state 'default'. Example: 'prod'.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Secret key name (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE recommended). Example: 'STRIPE_SECRET_KEY'.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Organization identifier for org-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='org'. Example: 'acme-corp'.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root for project-scoped secrets and policy resolution. Defaults to the MCP server's current working directory when omitted.

parameters.name: rotateEveryDays
parameters.description: Rotation reminder interval in days (1-3650). `inspect_secret` then reports rotation state ok / due-soon / overdue, and the dashboard and `qring rotate:due` surface it. Purely a reminder — nothing rotates automatically. Omit to keep the existing interval.

parameters.name: rotationFormat
parameters.description: Format used by `agent_scan --autoRotate` and `rotate_secret` when this secret expires. Pick the format that matches the upstream service's accepted shape.

parameters.name: rotationPrefix
parameters.description: Literal prefix prepended on auto-rotation (only used with rotationFormat 'api-key' or 'token'). Example: 'sk-'.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where the secret lives. 'global' = user keyring (default if omitted on reads), 'project' = scoped to projectPath, 'team' = team-shared (needs teamId), 'org' = org-shared (needs orgId).

parameters.name: tags

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Team identifier for team-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='team'. Example: 'acme-platform'.

parameters.name: ttlSeconds
parameters.description: Quantum decay window in seconds. After this many seconds the secret is marked expired (still readable, but `has_secret` returns false and `health_check` flags it). Omit for no decay.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The secret value to store. Stored as-is; never logged or echoed. May be empty only when `env` is provided to register a new env without a default.

tools.name: status_dashboard
tools.desc: [dashboard] Start a local web dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT`) that streams live KPIs, secret tables, manifest gaps,
tools.description: [dashboard] Start a local web dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT`) that streams live KPIs, secret tables, manifest gaps, hooks, audit events, and anomalies via Server-Sent Events. Use when an operator (or an agent on behalf of one) wants a richer visual surface than chat output; prefer `health_check` / `analyze_secrets` for one-shot text summaries inside the conversation. Side effect: binds an HTTP server on the requested port (one process-wide instance — re-running returns the existing URL instead of starting a second server). Never exposes secret values. Returns the URL string to open in a browser.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: TCP port to listen on (default 9876). Pick another port if 9876 is already in use; the call fails if binding errors.

tools.name: teleport_pack
tools.desc: [teleport] Encrypt one or more secrets into a single AES-256-GCM bundle string that can be safely transferred between ma
tools.description: [teleport] Encrypt one or more secrets into a single AES-256-GCM bundle string that can be safely transferred between machines. Use to hand off a curated set of credentials to another developer or environment; prefer `export_secrets` for plaintext .env output (single machine, trusted) and `tunnel_create` for ephemeral one-shot delivery on the same machine. Two modes, exactly one required: `passphrase` (v1, symmetric — receiver needs the same string) or `recipients` (v2, public-key — each receiver's `qring1...` string from `qring teleport identity`; no shared secret, only the listed identities can open it). Reads each secret value (records 'export' audit events) and produces a base64-encoded ciphertext. Returns the bundle string directly. Errors with 'No secrets to pack' if the filter matched zero secrets.

parameters.name: keys
parameters.description: Whitelist of exact key names to include. Omit to pack every secret in the requested scope.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Organization identifier for org-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='org'. Example: 'acme-corp'.

parameters.name: passphrase
parameters.description: Symmetric passphrase used to derive the AES-256-GCM key (v1 bundle). The receiver must supply the same string to `teleport_unpack`. Pick something high-entropy and share it out-of-band. Mutually exclusive with `recipients`.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root for project-scoped secrets and policy resolution. Defaults to the MCP server's current working directory when omitted.

parameters.name: recipients
parameters.description: Recipient public keys (`qring1...` strings, one per teammate) for a v2 recipient pack. The bundle can only be opened by the matching private keys, which each receiver created with `qring teleport keygen`. Mutually exclusive with `passphrase`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where the secret lives. 'global' = user keyring (default if omitted on reads), 'project' = scoped to projectPath, 'team' = team-shared (needs teamId), 'org' = org-shared (needs orgId).

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Team identifier for team-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='team'. Example: 'acme-platform'.

tools.name: teleport_unpack
tools.desc: [teleport] Decrypt a bundle produced by `teleport_pack` and import each contained secret into the local keyring. Use on
tools.description: [teleport] Decrypt a bundle produced by `teleport_pack` and import each contained secret into the local keyring. Use on the receiving machine after a packer hands you the bundle; prefer `dryRun=true` first to preview what will be written. Passphrase (v1) bundles need `passphrase`. Recipient (v2) bundles need no input: this machine's teleport identity is read from the OS keyring (create one with `qring teleport keygen`; the private key is never returned). When dryRun is false this mutates the keyring (one 'write' event per imported secret) at the requested scope. Bad passphrase, missing identity, not-a-recipient or tampered bundle returns JSON `{ ok: false, error: { message } }` with `isError: true`. On success returns 'Imported N secret(s) from teleport bundle'; in dryRun mode returns 'Would import N secrets:' followed by a `KEY [scope]` listing (v2 also lists the recipient ids the bundle is addressed to).

parameters.name: bundle
parameters.description: Base64-encoded ciphertext returned by `teleport_pack`. Pass through whitespace untouched if possible.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: If true, decrypt and report what would be written but do not mutate the keyring. Useful for verifying bundle contents before commit.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Organization identifier for org-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='org'. Example: 'acme-corp'.

parameters.name: passphrase
parameters.description: The passphrase used to pack a v1 bundle. Omit for v2 recipient bundles (decrypted with this machine's keyring identity). Bad passphrases return an authentication error rather than wrong plaintext.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root for project-scoped secrets and policy resolution. Defaults to the MCP server's current working directory when omitted.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where the secret lives. 'global' = user keyring (default if omitted on reads), 'project' = scoped to projectPath, 'team' = team-shared (needs teamId), 'org' = org-shared (needs orgId).

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Team identifier for team-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='team'. Example: 'acme-platform'.

tools.name: tunnel_create
tools.desc: [tunnel] Stash a one-shot or short-lived secret in the q-ring server's process memory and return an ID that can be used
tools.description: [tunnel] Stash a one-shot or short-lived secret in the q-ring server's process memory and return an ID that can be used to read it back. Use for handing a one-time value to another tool/process without persisting it (npm OTP codes, magic-link tokens, copy/paste between machines via a relay); prefer `set_secret` with `ttlSeconds` when you actually want a tracked, auditable secret. Mutates only in-memory state — the value never touches disk and is lost on server restart. Subject to tool policy. Returns JSON `{ ok, data: { id } }` where `id` is an opaque string to pass to `tunnel_read`/`tunnel_destroy`.

parameters.name: maxReads
parameters.description: Self-destruct after this many successful `tunnel_read` calls. Use 1 for true one-shot delivery.

parameters.name: ttlSeconds
parameters.description: Auto-destroy the tunnel after this many seconds. Omit for no time limit (then a `maxReads` is highly recommended).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The plaintext value to tunnel. Held only in process memory; never logged.

tools.name: tunnel_destroy
tools.desc: [tunnel] Immediately remove a tunnel from memory, regardless of remaining reads or TTL. Use when a tunneled value should
tools.description: [tunnel] Immediately remove a tunnel from memory, regardless of remaining reads or TTL. Use when a tunneled value should be cancelled before delivery (e.g. wrong recipient, secret already rotated); prefer letting `maxReads`/TTL handle cleanup for normal flows. Mutates in-memory state only. Returns 'Destroyed ID' on success or a not-found error if the ID is unknown or already gone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The opaque tunnel ID to destroy.

tools.name: tunnel_list
tools.desc: [tunnel] Enumerate all currently-active tunnels in the q-ring server with their remaining read budget and time-to-live.
tools.description: [tunnel] Enumerate all currently-active tunnels in the q-ring server with their remaining read budget and time-to-live. Use to audit what is still in memory or to look up an ID you forgot; values are never included in the output. Read-only. Returns one line per tunnel formatted as `id | reads:N | max:N | expires:Ns`, or the literal text 'No active tunnels' when the list is empty.

tools.name: tunnel_read
tools.desc: [tunnel] Fetch the value stashed by a prior `tunnel_create` call by its ID. Use exactly once per intended consumer; the
tools.description: [tunnel] Fetch the value stashed by a prior `tunnel_create` call by its ID. Use exactly once per intended consumer; the value is destructive-by-design and may self-delete after this call. Increments the read counter and may auto-destroy the tunnel if `maxReads` was set. Returns JSON `{ ok, data: { id, value } }` on success, or an error 'Tunnel "..." not found or expired' if the tunnel has been destroyed, hit its TTL, or never existed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The opaque tunnel ID returned by `tunnel_create`. Case-sensitive.

tools.name: validate_secret
tools.desc: [validation] Test whether a stored secret is still accepted by its upstream service (OpenAI, Stripe, GitHub, AWS, generi
tools.description: [validation] Test whether a stored secret is still accepted by its upstream service (OpenAI, Stripe, GitHub, AWS, generic HTTP, etc.) by making a minimal authenticated request. Use to confirm liveness before relying on a credential or as the verification step after `rotate_secret`; prefer `ci_validate_secrets` for a batch run across every key in scope. Side effects: makes one outbound network request per call (may incur tiny provider-side rate-limit cost). Records 'read' for the underlying secret value in the audit log; the value itself is never logged. Returns JSON `{ valid, provider, status?, message?, rateLimit?, ... }` (provider-specific shape).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The exact key whose value should be tested upstream. Example: 'OPENAI_API_KEY'.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Organization identifier for org-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='org'. Example: 'acme-corp'.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root for project-scoped secrets and policy resolution. Defaults to the MCP server's current working directory when omitted.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Force a specific provider id. Built-ins include 'openai', 'stripe', 'github', 'aws', 'http'. Omit to auto-detect from the value's prefix or the secret's stored provider hint.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Where the secret lives. 'global' = user keyring (default if omitted on reads), 'project' = scoped to projectPath, 'team' = team-shared (needs teamId), 'org' = org-shared (needs orgId).

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Team identifier for team-scoped secrets. Required only when scope='team'. Example: 'acme-platform'.

tools.name: verify_audit_chain
tools.desc: [audit] Recompute the SHA-256 hash chain over the audit log and confirm no event has been mutated, deleted, or reordered
tools.description: [audit] Recompute the SHA-256 hash chain over the audit log and confirm no event has been mutated, deleted, or reordered. Use periodically as a tamper-evidence check, or whenever you suspect the audit log has been touched outside q-ring; the result is informational — this tool does not repair the chain if it is broken. Read-only. Returns JSON `{ ok, valid, brokenAt? }` where `valid` is `true` for an intact chain and `brokenAt` (when present) names the first event whose hash did not match.

tools.description:
El índice de salarios estima la evolución de los salarios pagados en la economía aislando el indicador de variaciones relacionadas con conceptos tales como la cantidad de horas trabajadas, descuentos por ausentismo, premios por productividad y todo otro concepto asociado al desempeño o a las características de los individuos concretos.
 
La serie muestra la evolución de los salarios pagados en los sectores privado registrado y público desde noviembre de 2015. A partir de octubre de 2016 se incorporó la serie del sector privado no registrado y el cálculo del índice de salarios total, que resulta de la agregación de los índices de salarios de los componentes mencionados.
 
Para más información, se puede consultar la metodología INDEC N° 16, Índice de salarios y coeficiente de variación salarial, a través del siguiente enlace: https://www.indec.gob.ar/ftp/cuadros/sociedad/cvs_metodologia.pdf

tools.description:

tools.name: autoExpandNode
tools.desc: Generates follow-up prompts for the node's thread and creates them as `queued` child nodes, returning their ids — one ch
tools.description: Generates follow-up prompts for the node's thread and creates them as `queued` child nodes, returning their ids — one child per prompt. How many prompts is the model's call, read from the node's own thread, so it varies by node; there is nothing to size or steer. A level holds a handful, and wider material comes back grouped, one prompt per group, so its members arrive a level further down. One level only: the children are created `queued` and are not run, and nothing recurses. Each child runs only when it is submitted; until then it reads back as `interrupted`. A node that already has children is refused with 409 `node_has_children`. Metered by the usage gate against the token's user; over budget returns 429. Ownership is enforced.

tools.description: Runs the LLM on a node and returns the completed node — the first generative operation. The call BLOCKS: it waits until no ancestor is still generating (the generation gate, so the response always sees complete ancestor context and never races a parent that is mid-stream), then runs the generation to completion server-side and returns the finished node. Metered by the usage gate against the token's user once the generation gate clears; over budget returns 429. Submitting a node that already has children is refused with 409 (regenerating it would invalidate the descendant conversation paths) unless it is an expand node and `force=true`, which deletes those children first via the structural cascade. Ownership is enforced.

tools.desc:

cancellation payload. Supports batch cancellation
tools.description:
Cancels one or more open Hyperliquid orders using a pre-signed EIP-712
cancellation payload. Supports batch cancellation of up to 50 order IDs.
Scout capacity is available inside the shared 30 requests / 24h quota; Pioneer is capped at 1,500/day and Syndicate at 50,000/day. After the Scout quota, the default x402 overage is $0.01 USDC for one additional API call. Commercial capacity never supplies venue authority: every
cancellation request must include a fresh EIP-712 signature from the
user's Hyperliquid API wallet. For delegated signing, `accountAddress`
identifies the venue-verified equity owner. A subaccount/vault owner is
incorporated as `vaultAddress` in both the signature hash and exchange
request. FarmDash recovers the exact signer before submission. Required
`expiresAt` is forwarded as
Hyperliquid `expiresAfter`; required `intentHash` binds the FarmDash
request for auditability. HTTP 202 is returned only when Hyperliquid
supplies one explicit `success` application status per requested order;
this is `accepted` application acknowledgement, not final venue cancellation.
Mixed or total application errors are rejections. Reconcile every requested
ID through `/api/v1/agent/futures/reconcile-order` before dependent action.
Venue nonce authority is `network + signer + nonce` across account and vault
contexts. Durable replay control fails closed before submission.
WARNING: Real market actions can cause financial loss. USER_SIGNED requires fresh manual approval for each order/cancel. BOUNDED_AUTONOMOUS permits local agent signing without per-order confirmation only under a valid explicit owner-signed futures grant, authenticated session, venue delegation and all applicable gates. Read x-farmdash-capability-truth and live domain readiness; preparation or payment alone never authorizes dispatch.

tools.name: executeOrder
tools.desc:
Forwards a pre-signed EIP-712 order to Hyperliquid's exchange API.
Requires an execution-ready analyze-strategy call wit
tools.description:
Forwards a pre-signed EIP-712 order to Hyperliquid's exchange API.
Requires an execution-ready analyze-strategy call within 60 seconds. The
gate binds market, side, maximum size, 50 bps entry drift, maximum
analyzed leverage metadata, stop-derived risk, and the account whose
equity funded the sizing decision. `funding_arb` remains
analysis-only because this endpoint cannot atomically bind both legs.
Scout capacity is available inside the shared 30 requests / 24h quota; Pioneer is capped at 1,500/day and Syndicate at 50,000/day. After the Scout quota, the default x402 overage is $0.01 USDC for one additional API call. Commercial capacity never supplies venue authority: every request
must also include a fresh EIP-712 signature from the user's
Hyperliquid API wallet. All risk
guardrails enforced server-side before forwarding. `nonce`, `expiresAt`,
and `intentHash` are required for request-scoped expiry and auditability.
Venue nonce authority is `network + signer + nonce` across account and vault
contexts. Durable replay control fails closed before submission.
`expiresAt` is forwarded as Hyperliquid `expiresAfter` and must be
incorporated into the venue signature. The signed order action contains
the FarmDash builder term `f=1`, meaning 0.1 basis point (0.001%) of
filled notional—not 1 bp. The user must approve that builder fee on
Hyperliquid before execution. Rejected/resting/unfilled notional is not
reported as fee-bearing volume. FarmDash recovers the signer from the
exact signed L1 payload and rejects any mismatch with `agentAddress`.
When the verified owner is a Hyperliquid subaccount or vault,
`accountAddress` is also incorporated as the signed and submitted
`vaultAddress`; it cannot be changed after signing.
It also preflights the account owner's Hyperliquid `maxBuilderFee` and
blocks when the approved maximum is below `f=1`; only the main account
wallet, not an API wallet, can sign that approval action.
WARNING: Real market actions can cause financial loss. USER_SIGNED requires fresh manual approval for each order/cancel. BOUNDED_AUTONOMOUS permits local agent signing without per-order confirmation only under a valid explicit owner-signed futures grant, authenticated session, venue delegation and all applicable gates. Read x-farmdash-capability-truth and live domain readiness; preparation or payment alone never authorizes dispatch.

tools.description: Search the string-transformation utilities this server can run (246 total, across categories like Encoding, Hashing, Ciphers, Compression, Data Formats, Analysis, Generators and more). Returns {items: [{id, name, category, description}], total, categories}, best matches first. Use this first to find an id, then call describe_utility for its exact parameters before run_utility.

tools.name: run_pipeline
tools.desc: Run a whole pipeline — an ordered list of steps, in the string-utility-belt v2 schema, which may include branches (paral
tools.description: Run a whole pipeline — an ordered list of steps, in the string-utility-belt v2 schema, which may include branches (parallel forks merged back together) and macros (named sub-pipelines) — on `input`. Returns {output, outputEncoding?, errors, timings, skipped, halted}: `errors` maps step id to its error message, `timings` maps step id to milliseconds. Provide exactly one of `steps` or `share` (a `#/p/<payload>` share link, a full URL containing one, or the bare payload). Untrusted step data is sanitized first, so malformed entries are dropped rather than rejected. Refused outright: pipelines with more than 100 steps (branches/macros counted), unknown utility ids, enabled steps with invalid params, and any step that would run arbitrary user JavaScript (e.g. "custom_js") — LLM-driven code execution is out of scope. Input is capped at 1,000,000 bytes, output text past 1,000,000 characters is cut off (flagged `truncated`, with `fullLength`), and the call is stopped after 20s.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: The pipeline's source input.

parameters.name: inputEncoding
parameters.description: How to decode `input`. Default "text".

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share link (or its bare payload) for a previously built pipeline; used instead of `steps`.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: Pipeline steps (v2 schema). Each entry is either a utility step {id, utilityId, params?, enabled?, condition?, onError?}, a fork {type:"branch", id, branches:[[...steps], [...steps]], merge:{mode:"concat"|"zip"|"json"|"pick", ...}}, or a sub-pipeline {type:"macro", id, name, steps:[...steps]}. `condition` gates a step on its input ({kind:"always"|"nonEmpty"|"regex"|"type", ...}); `onError` is "passthrough" (default: record the error, pass the input on), "stop" or "empty". Use [] for the identity pipeline; omit when using `share`.

tools.name: run_utility
tools.desc: Run a single utility on `input` and return {output, outputEncoding?}. Plain text output is returned as-is; a JSON-produc
tools.description: Run a single utility on `input` and return {output, outputEncoding?}. Plain text output is returned as-is; a JSON-producing utility returns pretty-printed JSON text; a byte-producing utility (e.g. gzip_compress, get_bytes) returns base64 with `outputEncoding: "base64"`. `inputEncoding` controls how `input` itself is decoded first: "text" (default) uses it as-is, "base64" or "hex" decode it to raw bytes, "json" parses it. Params are validated against describe_utility's spec; invalid ones are rejected. Input is capped at 1,000,000 bytes, output text past 1,000,000 characters is cut off (flagged `truncated`, with `fullLength`), and the call is stopped after 20s. A failing utility returns isError with the error message. Utilities that run arbitrary user JavaScript (e.g. "custom_js") are refused, and the few that need a browser DOM parser (e.g. "xml_to_json", "html_table_to_csv") fail here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Utility id (see list_utilities / describe_utility).

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: The value to run the utility on.

parameters.name: inputEncoding
parameters.description: How to decode `input` before passing it to the utility. Default "text".

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Utility parameters (see describe_utility for names/kinds); params left out use their declared default.

tools.name: delete_api_v1_catalog_name
tools.desc: `mode=detach` (default) clears `catalog` on every member so it appears under Uncataloged, through a versioned write per
tools.description: `mode=detach` (default) clears `catalog` on every member so it appears under Uncataloged, through a versioned write per member. `mode=cascade` deletes every member tap and pipeline, including each pipeline's destination data, and requires `confirm` equal to `name`. Both remove every placeholder of the catalog (matched by its `catalog` field, or by name suffix when that field is empty). A member already moved out of `name` by a concurrent change is listed under `failed`. Not transactional: failed members are listed under `failed` (207). Catalog operations (rename, detach, cascade) are serialized server-side, so concurrent requests run one after another and the later one sees the earlier one's result. Requires `pipeline:delete`; each member is also checked against the key's owner and catalog scopes, and the placeholder is left untouched if any member is refused. In cascade mode, if any tap delete fails, the catalog's pipelines are not deleted and are reported under `failed`. A cascade response also carries `warnings` (always present, possibly empty): one entry per deleted pipeline that needs a follow-up, such as a Unity Catalog table Datris could not drop; warnings never change the status code. Refused with 409 while an ordered enable of the catalog (`POST /api/v1/catalog/{name}/enable-ordered`) is running.

parameters.description: Required for `mode=cascade`; must equal the catalog name.

tools.description: Starts one server-side job that walks the catalog's enable order (see `GET /api/v1/catalog/{name}/enable-order`) level by level, one tap at a time. Per tap: if any of its dependencies failed, was skipped or cancelled, or has not landed data, the tap is `skipped` with the reason; otherwise it is tested when it has no passing test (a failed test marks it `failed`), enabled (the test-before-cron gate applies; a refusal marks it `failed` with that text), given one real run (an error or zero records marks it `failed`) and the job waits until the run's pipeline loads have finished (`success`/`warning` = `landed`, `error` = `failed`, no finish within `datris.catalog.enableWaitMs`, default 30 minutes = `failed`). A tap that was already enabled with landed data is not re-run. No request body. Requires `tap:run`; the key must also hold `tap:update` and `tap:run` for every member tap (owner and catalog scope), otherwise 403 and nothing starts. Agent policy action `tap:run:enable-ordered` (inherits `tap:run`): an approval covers the whole job.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Catalog name. `Uncataloged` (any case) is refused.

tools.name: post_api_v1_catalog_name_restore
tools.desc: Restores an archive produced by `GET /api/v1/catalog/{name}/export` as catalog `name` (the same or a new name, on the sa
tools.description: Restores an archive produced by `GET /api/v1/catalog/{name}/export` as catalog `name` (the same or a new name, on the same or another install). A restore never merges: with `mode=new` (default) it is refused with 409 when catalog `name` already exists or any archived tap or pipeline name exists anywhere on the install (any catalog, either type), and nothing is written. With `mode=overwrite` (requires `confirm` equal to `name`) items already in `name` may be replaced; a name in another catalog is still a 409. When tap scripts are stored in a code repository, a script file already at branch head with different content is also a clash; identical content is reused without a new commit. Pipelines are saved exactly as `POST /api/v1/pipeline` saves them; tap scripts go to the install's default script storage; taps are saved with `enabled=false` and their run status cleared, so nothing runs until a user tests and enables them. Secrets are never written: `missingSecrets` lists the secrets the archived items reference that are absent on this install. Secrets are only checked where the key may read them: a key without secret read access gets a `<name>: not checked, this key may not read secrets` warning instead, whether or not the secret exists. Each tap's incremental state is restored for taps that did not exist before, unless `restoreState=false`. An archive with no members creates the empty catalog. Not transactional: failed members are listed under `failed` (207). Requires `pipeline:create`. Every member is scope-checked before anything is written: `tap:create` / `pipeline:create` in the target catalog as the caller, and for an item that already exists (overwrite) also `tap:update` / `pipeline:update` against its current catalog and owner. A refused member is listed under `failed` and nothing of it, including its validation schema, is written. Inline credentials (preprocessor and REST destination `bearerToken`/`apiKey`, `restEndpoint` row-function token parameters) are removed at export; the restore response's `warnings` names each one to re-enter. Refused with 409 while an ordered enable of the catalog (`POST /api/v1/catalog/{name}/enable-ordered`) is running.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Required for `mode=overwrite`; must equal the catalog name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Target catalog name. `Uncataloged` (any case) is refused.

parameters.name: regenerateScripts
parameters.description: By default each pipeline's archived AI scripts become its live scripts, with no model call. `true` regenerates them on this install instead. An archived script with no `.json` record, or whose record no longer matches the archived pipeline's instruction and source schema or this server's script contract, is regenerated either way (or, when the pipeline already has a live script that matches, kept); `scriptsRegenerated` and `scriptsKept` name each with the reason.

parameters.name: restoreState
parameters.description: `false` skips every tap's incremental state (for a copy that should start from scratch).

tools.desc: Saves (upserts) a pipeline configuration. Invalid field protection is rejected at save time (unknown or not-yet-supporte
tools.description: Saves (upserts) a pipeline configuration. Invalid field protection is rejected at save time (unknown or not-yet-supported `protect.method`, `preserve` outside `mask`, a string-producing method on a non-string field, any method but `hmac` on a `keyFields` column, or a source that is not delimited or JSON). Like every other validator error, the rejection returns HTTP 400 with `{"error": "..."}` naming the field.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
Destination configuration (database, objectStore, kafka, activeMQ, restEndpoint, qdrant, weaviate, milvus, chroma, pgvector).

The database destination selects its engine with exactly one of `usePostgres`, `useMongoDB`, `useSnowflake`, `useDatabricks`, or `useSqlServer` (boolean, default `false`). Snowflake and Databricks additionally take `credentialsSecret` (a Platform secret) and `warehouse` (Snowflake warehouse name / Databricks SQL warehouse ID); for Databricks, `dbName` names the Unity Catalog catalog. For Databricks, `warehouse` may be omitted when the credentials secret has a `warehouse` field (aliases `httpPath`, `http_path`, `DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE`). `useSqlServer` loads a Microsoft SQL Server or Azure SQL database and requires `credentialsSecret` (a Platform secret with `host`, optional `port`, and `authMethod` — `sql` (default): `user`, `password`; `entraServicePrincipal`: `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `tenantId`; `entraPassword`: `user`, `password`; `entraManagedIdentity`: optional `managedIdentityClientId`; `kerberos`: `principal` plus either `password` or `jaasConfigurationName` (keytab)); `dbName` is the database on that server and `schema` is usually `dbo`. It accepts CSV, JSON (single `_json` field) and XML (single `_xml` field) sources.

objectStore supports two providers via the `provider` field: `minio` (default, uses the built-in MinIO credentials) and `s3` (AWS S3). For `provider: s3`, set `destinationBucketOverride` (required), `credentialsSecret` (Vault secret with `accessKey`/`secretKey`/`region` and optional `sessionToken`), and optionally `endpoint` (must be https://). Region lives in the credentials secret, not on the objectStore config.

`fileFormat` accepts `parquet` (default), `orc`, or `iceberg`; with `iceberg`, `writeMode` may also be `merge`, which upserts on the `keyFields` array (each a destination schema column).

restEndpoint takes `endpoint`, `async`, `bearerToken`, `apiKey`, `timeoutMs` and an optional `batchSize` (default `0` = one call carrying every row). With `batchSize > 0`, row-based payloads are POSTed in batches of that many rows, each request also carrying top-level `batch` (1-based) and `ofBatches`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Pipeline name

parameters.name: preprocessor
parameters.description: Optional REST endpoint preprocessor (`endpoint`, `async`, `bearerToken`, `apiKey`, `timeoutMs`, `batchSize`). `batchSize` defaults to `0` (one call carrying every row, whose response `data` replaces the payload). With `batchSize > 0`, row-based payloads are POSTed in batches of that many rows — each request also carrying top-level `batch` (1-based) and `ofBatches` — and every response's `data.rows` are stitched, in call order, into the payload passed downstream.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source configuration (fileAttributes, schemaProperties)

fields.description: Source fields. A field may carry `protect`; see Field Protection in the docs.

parameters.name: transformation
parameters.description:
Transformation rules (AI transformation, deduplication, row functions).

`rowFunctions` is an array of `{ "function", "parameters" }`. For `"function": "restEndpoint"` the positional `parameters` are `[url, mode, timeoutMs, bearerToken, apiKey, batchSize]`: `mode` is `"row"` (default; one call per row carrying `{pipelineName, pipelineToken, row}`, a `null` row in the response removes it) or `"batch"` (calls carry `{pipelineName, pipelineToken, rows}`). In batch mode the optional sixth parameter `batchSize` (default `0`) sets the rows per call: `0` makes one call carrying every row; `> 0` sends ceil(rows / batchSize) calls of that many rows, in source order, and stitches the responses in call order. Only `url` is required.

tools.name: post_api_v1_pipeline_dest-types
tools.desc: Applies column types to an all-string destination. Destination-first: if data has already landed the table is migrated b
tools.description: Applies column types to an all-string destination. Destination-first: if data has already landed the table is migrated before the config changes — postgres retypes in place; sqlserver validates every landed value with TRY_CONVERT and then retypes in place with ALTER COLUMN in one transaction (its `_json` / `_xml` document columns are never retyped); snowflake/databricks validate every landed value with TRY_CAST and then swap the table. Any landed value that will not cast fails the whole apply with the column named and nothing changed. On success the pipeline definition is updated as a new version. The migration locks or replaces the table — do not apply while a run is in flight.

tools.description: Generates a new script for `kind` now, from the source schema, with the current CodeGen model, and replaces the stored one. If generation fails the error is returned (502) and the current script stays in place. For a JSON or XML pipeline the script is marked pending and the next run generates it from its data. A repository-backed script whose file was edited in the repository since the recorded commit is not overwritten (409) unless `overwrite=true`. The new script is a new version in the script's history. A built-in script object is replaced; a repository-backed script gets a new commit. The pipeline's definition version does not change. When the version's text is already the live script, nothing is written (no version, no commit) and the current entry is returned with `noop: true`. tools.description: Execute a read-only T-SQL query (SELECT or WITH; metadata through INFORMATION_SCHEMA views) against the SQL Server or Azure SQL destination of a pipeline. tools.description: Internal callback, not a client API. tools.name: post_api_v1_tap

Cron validation: `cronExpression` is a Quartz expres
tools.description:
Creates a new tap or updates an existing tap with the same `name`.

Cron validation: `cronExpression` is a Quartz expression of 6 fields
(seconds minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week) plus an optional
year. A malformed expression — including the 5-field Unix form — is
refused with 400 and nothing is persisted; for a 5-field input the error
carries the 6-field equivalent to resend. A blank cron means unscheduled.

Test-before-cron: a `cronExpression` may only be saved once the exact script
(or HTTP endpoint) that will run on it has passed a `mode=test` run. Setting or
changing a cron on an untested script, or changing the script under an existing
cron, is refused with 409 and nothing is persisted. Remedy: save without
`cronExpression`, run `POST /api/v1/tap/run` with `mode=test`, then save again
with the cron.

parameters.description: Label of the API key that created the tap; stamped by the server and used for owner-scoped capability checks

parameters.name: cronExpression
parameters.description: Quartz CRON expression for scheduled runs (omit for manual-only). Six fields — seconds minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week — plus an optional year, e.g. `0 0 * * * ?` (hourly). A 5-field Unix cron such as `*/1 * * * *` is rejected with 400; the error quotes the 6-field equivalent.

parameters.description:
Taps of the same catalog whose destination tables this tap reads, declared by the user.
When set (even `[]`, meaning "none") it replaces `inferredDependsOn`. Omitted on an update:

and the list may not close a dependency cycle (409 with `cycle`). Orders and explains the
catalog's enable order only; never enforced on save, test, run or schedule.

tools.name: put_api_v1_catalog_name
tools.desc: Relabels every tap and pipeline whose `catalog` equals `name` to `newName`, each through a versioned write (one new defi
tools.description: Relabels every tap and pipeline whose `catalog` equals `name` to `newName`, each through a versioned write (one new definition version per member, with a change note naming the rename and the actor). Every hidden placeholder of the catalog (a `__catalog__*` tap whose `catalog` field is `name`, or whose name suffix is `name` when that field is empty) is removed, and `__catalog__<newName>` is created with `catalog=newName`. A member already moved out of `name` by a concurrent change is listed under `failed` ("no longer in catalog"), and placeholders are left untouched when no member moved. A rename never merges: if `newName` already exists (any tap or pipeline carries it, or it has a placeholder; matched case-sensitively) the request is refused with 409 and nothing changes. To combine catalogs, move their items. Not transactional: members that fail are listed under `failed` and the rest still move (207). API keys whose capabilities are scoped `catalog=<name>` are listed under `affectedKeys`; their scopes are not rewritten. Catalog operations (rename, detach, cascade) are serialized server-side, so concurrent requests run one after another and the later one sees the earlier one's result. Requires `pipeline:update`; each member is also checked against the key's owner and catalog scopes. If any member is refused by scope, placeholders are left untouched (`placeholder: skipped`); for a catalog with only a placeholder, the placeholder is scope-checked (403 on denial). Refused with 409 while an ordered enable of the catalog (`POST /api/v1/catalog/{name}/enable-ordered`) is running.

tools.description: Stores a file via multipart upload and returns a download link. Only safe file types accepted; a missing or wrong extension is corrected from the content and reported in notices. Reuse existing owner token to group entities under one owner. An HTML or Markdown file is published as a page in any namespace, with or without a password (same rules and limits as POST /api/html). 'format' decides; without one a known extension, then a specific declared part type (text/html, text/markdown, application/json, text/csv), then a content guess; otherwise it stays an inert file. '.txt' without 'format' stays a text file. A whole HTML document sent as 'markdown' is an HTML page. Any readable encoding is stored as UTF-8, notice 'charset-guessed' when no usable charset was named. link and ownerLink point to the page, notice 'html-file-as-page' or 'markdown-file-as-page'; a code format chosen by 'format' or the declared type is published the same way, notice 'file-format-applied'. An HTML file over the page size limit or that no encoding reads is stored as a file and shown as source, notice 'html-file-as-source'. A JSON file in the public namespace is stored as sent, notice 'json-file-not-listed'; JSON data belongs in POST /api/json. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password.

tools.description: Commit to actually try a recipe and report the outcome within the contract window (7 days; sooner is better). Without accept_contract, or without a key, nothing is recorded: it returns the contract terms and what to do next. Use it when you will run the recipe; to just read, use get_recipe. tools.description: Create a free bot account so your downloads and reports are attributed to you: pass handle and signature and the API key comes back immediately (shown once; store it in BOTGATHERING_API_KEY). New bots start UNVERIFIED: downloads and reports work, but reports move recipe scores only after verification (one honest on-time report_result, or an email link your human clicks). Other modes, picked from the arguments: email + api_key (no handle) requests a verification link for an existing bot; handle + api_key (no email) renames an anonymous anon-... account; email + code completes a legacy 6-digit code. tools.description: Show your own bot account: handle, signature, verified flag and verification status, reliability with counts (due, on_time, overdue, pending) and open obligations, i.e. recipes you downloaded but have not reported yet, each with report_token, due date and status for report_result. tools.name: analysis_anomalies_check
tools.desc: Detect anomalies for one campaign by comparing its current metrics against a median-based baseline built from STATE.json
tools.description: Detect anomalies for one campaign by comparing its current metrics against a median-based baseline built from STATE.json's action_log history. Returns severity-ordered anomalies — zero spend (CRITICAL), CPA spike (HIGH/CRITICAL, gated by 30+ conversions), CTR drop (HIGH/CRITICAL, gated by 1000+ impressions). No baseline is produced when history < min_baseline_entries (default 7).

tools.name: analysis_delivery_collapse_check
tools.desc: Detect delivery collapse: campaigns whose impressions fell off a cliff while their status still says they should be serv
tools.description: Detect delivery collapse: campaigns whose impressions fell off a cliff while their status still says they should be serving. The inverse of google_ads_cost_increase_investigate, and the scheduled detector /daily-check runs. Feed it a day-grain delivery report (one row per campaign per day, ~30+ days) for ANY platform — hosted connectors, bridges and plugins included. The baseline is the median of the SAME WEEKDAY from those rows, so weekend dips do not fire, and it never reads action_log, so it works on accounts operated partly by hand. The current (partial) day is always excluded. Thresholds come from STRATEGY.md ## Guardrails (delivery_collapse_drop_pct, delivery_collapse_consecutive_days, delivery_collapse_min_baseline_impressions, delivery_collapse_baseline_days) and default to a 90% drop against a 28-day baseline. Read-only.

tools.description: analysis_delivery_collapse_diagnose

tools.name: analysis_exclusion_impact_preview
tools.desc: Before applying a batch of exclusions / blocks / negative keywords, report how much of the account's OWN recent delivery
tools.description: Before applying a batch of exclusions / blocks / negative keywords, report how much of the account's OWN recent delivery (impressions, clicks, cost, conversions) it removes — both for this batch and cumulatively for every standing exclusion once it lands. Call it with 'tool' + 'arguments' to size the exact call you are about to make on a surface mureo models (Google Ads negative placements / negative keywords, Meta excluded placements, plus any surface a plugin registered), or with 'excluded_entities' + 'delivery_records' to size a batch on any other platform from a report you fetched yourself — that form reaches no platform API. Returns coverage 'measured', 'partial' or 'unknown'; 'unknown' is an honest answer and never means 'no impact'. 'would_block' is computed by the same rule the dispatcher enforces from STRATEGY.md ## Guardrails, so it cannot disagree with what will actually happen. 'unevaluated_rules' names any guardrail the operator wrote that cannot be evaluated for this call — an inert rule is not a satisfied one, so surface it to the operator.

tools.name: analysis_tracking_consistency_check
tools.desc: Audit final-URL tracking parameters across ad records you pass in, on any platform. Returns findings with severity, deli
tools.description: Audit final-URL tracking parameters across ad records you pass in, on any platform. Returns findings with severity, delivery_state (served / not_served / unknown), the ad ids involved and the evidence — ads carrying a utm scheme that belongs to exactly one other campaign, ads sending one landing page to two different schemes, ads missing a parameter the rest of their campaign carries, and violations of a '## Tracking Convention' declared in STRATEGY.md. Read-only; reaches no platform API. Pass planned_ads to pre-flight ads before creating them — then only the new ads are reported. Recognises utm_* parameters unless the convention declares more; ads with no readable URL are listed in ads_without_readable_url rather than reported clean.

tools.description: Return the loaded brand kit (colours, fonts, logo path, and logo clear-space) read from ./BRAND_KIT/kit.yml. When no kit exists, tasteful neutral defaults are returned and 'defaults_used' is true. Use this to judge brand fit before composing banners.

tools.name: creative_studio_compose
tools.desc: Composite ad copy + brand kit over a key visual into per-format banner PNGs. The typography layer: headline/body/CTA/bad
tools.description: Composite ad copy + brand kit over a key visual into per-format banner PNGs. The typography layer: headline/body/CTA/badge/logo are laid out in HTML/CSS and rendered by headless Chromium so Japanese text is pixel-perfect. Pick a layout 'template', the target 'formats', and pass the copy; the composed PNGs land in a new run directory with a provenance manifest. Requires the 'creative' extra (pip install 'mureo[creative]').

tools.name: creative_studio_edit_visual
tools.desc: Refine an existing key visual through an image provider's edit path (the art-direction loop: fix a weak visual, then re-
tools.description: Refine an existing key visual through an image provider's edit path (the art-direction loop: fix a weak visual, then re-score). The instruction describes the imagery change ONLY — no text is rendered by the model. The edited PNG is written next to the input as '<stem>_edit_<k>.png' and validated; the tool returns its path, SHA-256, and the provider used.

tools.name: creative_studio_generate_visual
tools.desc: Generate text-free key-visual PNGs for an ad creative. The prompt describes the imagery ONLY — headline/body/CTA text is
tools.description: Generate text-free key-visual PNGs for an ad creative. The prompt describes the imagery ONLY — headline/body/CTA text is added later by the typography layer, so a hard no-text constraint is appended automatically. Images are written to a new run directory with a provenance manifest.json; the tool returns the run id, directory, file paths (with SHA-256), and manifest path. Use 'provider' to pick one configured provider, or 'all' to fan out one image per configured provider.

tools.name: creative_studio_providers_list
tools.desc: List the image-generation providers available to Creative Studio. Each entry reports its name, whether it is configured
tools.description: List the image-generation providers available to Creative Studio. Each entry reports its name, whether it is configured (an API key in the credential store / env var, or — for the local Codex CLI provider — no key at all, just `codex login`), its capabilities, and its model ids. In capabilities, 'edit' is edit-path support, 'max_size' is the per-axis maximum ([max width, max height]) and NOT necessarily a generatable size, and the optional 'supported_sizes' is the exact [width, height] menu the provider renders (other requests are clamped to it); its absence means arbitrary sizes up to max_size. Call this before creative_studio_generate_visual to see which providers can be selected.

tools.description: Lists ad groups in a Google Ads account, optionally scoped to a single parent campaign and/or filtered by status. tools.description: Updates one or more settings on an existing ad group. Partial update — only provided fields are changed. Returns the updated ad group. Mutating — not automatically reversible; record before-state with mureo_state_action_log_append if you may need to roll back. Does not cascade to ads or keywords under this ad group; use google_ads_ads_update / update_status and google_ads.keywords.* for those.

tools.name: google_ads_ad_performance_compare
tools.desc: Rank ENABLED ads within a single Google Ads ad group and assign WINNER / LOSER / INSUFFICIENT_DATA verdicts. Returns {ad
tools.description: Rank ENABLED ads within a single Google Ads ad group and assign WINNER / LOSER / INSUFFICIENT_DATA verdicts. Returns {ad_group_id, period, ads:[{ad_id, impressions, clicks, conversions, cost, ctr, cvr, cpa, score (ctr*cvr, or ctr when conversions=0), rank, verdict, headlines?, descriptions?}], winner, recommendation, insights:[strings]}. Ads with impressions < 100 are flagged INSUFFICIENT_DATA; all ads tied at the top score receive WINNER, the rest LOSER. Read-only — does not pause or rotate ads. For cross-ad-group per-ad reporting use google_ads_ad_performance_report; for RSA asset-level splits use google_ads_rsa_assets_analyze.

tools.name: google_ads_ad_performance_report
tools.desc: Report per-ad performance across Google Ads ad_group_ad rows. Returns one row per ad shaped as {ad_id, ad_type, status (
tools.description: Report per-ad performance across Google Ads ad_group_ad rows. Returns one row per ad shaped as {ad_id, ad_type, status ('ENABLED'|'PAUSED'|'REMOVED'), ad_group_id, ad_group_name, campaign_id, campaign_name, metrics} where metrics contains impressions, clicks, cost_micros, cost (currency), conversions, ctr, average_cpc_micros, average_cpc, cost_per_conversion_micros, cost_per_conversion. Filterable by ad_group_id and/or campaign_id (both optional, both numeric). Read-only; no mutation. For ENABLED-only A/B comparison within a single ad group with WINNER/LOSER verdicts use google_ads_ad_performance_compare; for campaign-level aggregates use google_ads_performance_report.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_create
tools.desc: Creates a Responsive Search Ad (RSA) in the specified ad group. Returns the new ad's resource_name, id, and initial appr
tools.description: Creates a Responsive Search Ad (RSA) in the specified ad group. Returns the new ad's resource_name, id, and initial approval_status (usually UNDER_REVIEW for ~1 business day). Mutating — not automatically reversible; record before-state with mureo_state_action_log_append if you may need to roll back. Google Ads requires 3–15 headlines and 2–4 descriptions. For display/banner ads use google_ads_ads_create_display instead; the two creative formats are not interchangeable.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_create_display
tools.desc: Creates a Responsive Display Ad (RDA) in a DISPLAY campaign's ad group. Marketing/square/logo image paths point to local
tools.description: Creates a Responsive Display Ad (RDA) in a DISPLAY campaign's ad group. Marketing/square/logo image paths point to local files; mureo uploads each file to Google Ads as an ImageAsset before composing the ad. Returns the new ad's resource_name, id, and the generated asset IDs. Mutating — not automatically reversible; record before-state with mureo_state_action_log_append if you may need to roll back. For Search campaigns use google_ads_ads_create; the ad_group must belong to a DISPLAY campaign or this call fails with a channel-mismatch error.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_list
tools.desc: Lists ads in a Google Ads account, optionally scoped to one ad group and/or filtered by status. Returns id, ad_group_id,
tools.description: Lists ads in a Google Ads account, optionally scoped to one ad group and/or filtered by status. Returns id, ad_group_id, status, type (RESPONSIVE_SEARCH_AD / RESPONSIVE_DISPLAY_AD / etc.), final_urls, approval_status, and a creative summary (headlines / descriptions for RSAs). Read-only. Use this to find an ad_id before calling ads.update / update_status or to audit creative inventory. For disapproval details, follow up with google_ads_ads_policy_details.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_policy_details
tools.desc: Fetches the Google Ads policy review result for a single ad, including approval_status (APPROVED / APPROVED_LIMITED / DI
tools.description: Fetches the Google Ads policy review result for a single ad, including approval_status (APPROVED / APPROVED_LIMITED / DISAPPROVED / UNDER_REVIEW), a list of policy_topic_entries with topic (e.g. DESTINATION_NOT_WORKING, RESTRICTED_CONTENT), evidence, and an appeal eligibility flag. Read-only. Call this after google_ads_ads_list surfaces a non-APPROVED ad to understand the specific disapproval reasons.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_update
tools.desc: Updates the creative copy of an existing Responsive Search Ad by replacing headlines and/or descriptions. A supplied sid
tools.description: Updates the creative copy of an existing Responsive Search Ad by replacing headlines and/or descriptions. A supplied side is fully replaced (Google has no per-asset patch); omit a side to leave it unchanged — the omitted side is read from the current ad and preserved, so updating headlines never wipes descriptions. Returns the updated ad. Google Ads does not support in-place edit of RSA creative assets — this call typically replaces the ad with a new one under the same ID, which resets learning and triggers re-review. Mutating — not automatically reversible; record before-state with mureo_state_action_log_append if you may need to roll back. For status-only changes (pause/resume) use google_ads_ads_update_status, which is lighter-weight and does not reset learning.

tools.name: google_ads_ads_update_status
tools.desc: Sets the delivery status of a single ad to ENABLED, PAUSED, or REMOVED. Lightweight — writes only the status field and d
tools.description: Sets the delivery status of a single ad to ENABLED, PAUSED, or REMOVED. Lightweight — writes only the status field and does not reset learning signals. Returns the ad ID and new status. Reversible via rollback_apply. Use this for pause/resume; use google_ads_ads_update to change the creative copy itself.

tools.name: google_ads_asset_group_assets_list
tools.desc: Lists the text AND the images attached to Performance Max asset groups. Read-only. This is the tool for P-MAX creative:
tools.description: Lists the text AND the images attached to Performance Max asset groups. Read-only. This is the tool for P-MAX creative: google_ads_ads_list returns no rows for a Performance Max campaign because P-MAX has no ad_group_ad — its headlines and its pictures alike live on asset_group_asset. It is also the only way to say WHICH asset group serves a given image; google_ads_image_assets_list is account-wide and does not. Returns one entry per link. Every entry carries {resource_name (the asset_group_asset handle), field_type, status (the LINK status: 'ENABLED' | 'PAUSED' | 'REMOVED'), asset_id, asset_group_id, asset_group_name, campaign_id, campaign_resource_name}. field_type says what the rest of the entry holds: a text link ('HEADLINE' | 'LONG_HEADLINE' | 'DESCRIPTION') adds {text}; an image link ('MARKETING_IMAGE' | 'SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE' | 'PORTRAIT_MARKETING_IMAGE' | 'LOGO' | 'LANDSCAPE_LOGO') adds {asset_name, url (the full-size serving URL — fetch it to actually look at the creative), width_pixels, height_pixels}. Entries are returned in the order the API returned them and are not deduplicated — two links carrying the same asset are two entries, because that is what the asset group has. Video, business name and other field types are not returned. Pass the asset_id of the entry you want to change to google_ads_asset_group_assets_replace (text) or google_ads_asset_group_images_replace (images).

tools.name: google_ads_asset_group_assets_replace
tools.desc: Swaps one headline, long headline or description of a Performance Max asset group for new text. Mutating. A Google Ads t
tools.description: Swaps one headline, long headline or description of a Performance Max asset group for new text. Mutating. A Google Ads text Asset is immutable, so this creates a new Asset, links it to the asset group under the same field_type, and removes the old link — all three in ONE atomic GoogleAdsService.mutate, so the asset group's asset count for that field type never dips below the Performance Max minimum (a removal issued on its own is refused with AssetGroupError.NOT_ENOUGH_*). The old Asset itself is not deleted; only its link to this asset group is. Returns {asset_group_id, field_type, added: {asset_id, asset_resource_name, text, asset_group_asset}, removed: {asset_id, text, asset_group_asset}, note}. Not automatically reversible — to swap back, call this tool again with the old text; record before-state with mureo_state_action_log_append if you may need to roll back. Call google_ads_asset_group_assets_list first to get old_asset_id.

tools.name: google_ads_asset_group_images_replace
tools.desc: Swaps one image or logo of a Performance Max asset group for another. Mutating. Use this whichever situation you are in:
tools.description: Swaps one image or logo of a Performance Max asset group for another. Mutating.
